title: Native lane fetch-cache override breaks Windows configure
body: Exporting VIXEN_FETCHCONTENT_CACHE=<worktree>/.tmp/fetch (the WSL-side rule for Linux builds) before tools/vixen-native.sh makes the native configure use a //wsl.localhost UNC path; cmd.exe cannot cd into UNC, so glm populate fails and the stale glm-subbuild also poisons the later WSL configure. vixen-native.sh already defaults the cache into the native checkout. Suggested consolidation: vixen-native.sh should ignore or refuse a non-drive VIXEN_FETCHCONTENT_CACHE with a located message, and the lane rules should say the cache variable is for WSL builds only.

title: Native capture 'before' baseline must be built from the lane's own base
body: A pre-existing exe from lane-framecpu1 (merge-base 46c2670b) looked like a ready before-build but differs in pixels from the wave base 4d202765 (126619 of 250000 px, max delta 192), so a 'pixels changed' alarm was a base mismatch. Suggested consolidation: a capture-compare helper that records the source commit of each exe (and refuses a pair whose merge-base differs), or a shared base native checkout per wave commit.

title: Partial WSL Debug build misses the gpu-witness layer target
body: Building only libraries/RenderGraph/tests/all leaves libVkLayer_vixen_gpu_witness.so unbuilt, so BodyOctreeLifetimeTest.RealNodeRingLifecycleHasNoValidationErrors fails with 'cannot open shared object file' (passes once vixen_gpu_witness_layer is built). Suggested consolidation: make the tests that load the layer depend on its target (add_dependencies) so a suite-directory build is self-sufficient.

title: Benchmark and build jobs wait 20 to 110 min behind other lanes' bench windows
body: sn-framebase1 cap and build jobs sat in head-order / pinned-drain / bench-window-closing for about 3 h in total (drain estimates 1500 to 7000 s that kept growing); a pair of replicates as separate jobs would have cost 6 windows. Suggested consolidation: let a bench job that is a handful of short captures be admitted in the next window regardless of drain estimates, and show an ETA that does not grow.
